uncited: Transfer Function and Color Mapping defines the mechanism by which scalar, vector, or multivariate data values at sample points are mapped to visual attributes such as color, opacity, and brightness for volume rendering.

It solves the problem of perceptual encoding, allowing users to distinguish specific data features (e.g., high-velocity regions, conserved genomic sequences, or complex phases) that would otherwise be indistinguishable in raw data.

This family is distinct from sibling methods like [Stream Lines](4796-stream-lines.md) or [Glyph-based Vector/Tensor Visualization](10535-glyph-based-vector-tensor-visualization.md) because it operates directly on the volumetric data density, mapping values to optical properties for ray-casting or texture-based rendering rather than extracting geometric primitives or topological features.
**Step:** Store gradient values in a 1D texture on GPU.
Calculate three similarity plots: (a) all four species, (b) primates (human/chimp), (c) rodents (mouse/rat). 2.
This foundational work allowed for the visualization of internal structures in volumetric data, such as medical CT scans.
The specific techniques detailed in this family have evolved to address multivariate and complex data types.
